appraisal_events.evidence: les plus brillants d'entre eux la tenant un peu à l'écart... elle n'avait jamais reçu une invitation ni une visite de sa jeune cousine la princesse des Laumes, depuis six ans... elle avait fini par croire que c'était en effet la raison pour laquelle elle n'allait pas chez sa jeune cousine; the narrator dissects her repetitive 'chez mes cousins de Guermantes' idiom as a compensatory tic.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Gallardon's pride in her Guermantes kinship as a defensive compensation for being kept at arm's length by the more brilliant Guermantes and slighted by her cousin, revealing self-deceiving rationalization and an obsessive, repetitive social vocabulary.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Cambremer, comme elle avait très peu de relations, étant d'autant plus heureuse d'avoir une compagne, Mme de Franquetot, qui était au contraire très lancée, trouvait quelque chose d'élégant, d'original, à montrer à toutes ses belles connaissances qu'elle leur préférait une dame obscure avec qui elle avait en commun des souvenirs de jeunesse.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames Mme de Cambremer as socially thin and dependent on companionship, while her more fashionable cousin Mme de Franquetot treats the friendship as a stylish affectation that showcases her own originality, comparatively favoring Franquetot over Cambremer.

status_effects.explanation: Gallardon is exposed as an insecure, self-deceiving snob whose pride in her Guermantes kinship rests on thin, obsessively repeated material.
She is kept at a distance by the more brilliant Guermantes and passed over by her cousin's non-invitation despite her claimed closeness.
She is portrayed as having very few connections and as dependent on her cousin's companionship at gatherings.
She gains local social distinction by treating her preference for an 'obscure' cousin as a display of elegance and originality before her fashionable acquaintances.

ambiguities: The surface form 'la marquise de Cambremer' / 'Mme de Cambremer' is ambiguous per the reference sheet between Mme de Cambremer (née Legrandin, the marquis's wife) and the dowager marquise (his mother). Because this scene occurs within the 'Un Amour de Swann' flashback, well before the Legrandin-born marquise's marriage into the family, the dowager reading (la marquise douairière de Cambremer) is preferred here, though the sheet itself leaves the bare form unresolved rather than guessed.
